method: The sheet is described in millimetres. The text area is the chosen paper size minus the margin on every side, with landscape swapping the two page dimensions. Lined sheets place a horizontal rule every spacing interval from the first interval below the top margin to the bottom of the text area. Dot and graph sheets build the same square lattice: the column and row counts are the text width and height divided by the spacing, and the lattice is centred so leftover space is split evenly on both sides. Graph sheets draw every fifth row and column slightly heavier. Cornell sheets rule only the note area above a summary band at 74% of the text height and add a heavier divider at 30% of the text width for the cue column. Each page is an independent SVG with the page size set through @page, so print output at 100% keeps the requested millimetre spacing. Nothing is measured, stored, uploaded or sent, and no account is needed.
